root_cause.text: The rfkill_block work item was not canceled during wiphy_unregister(), allowing a use-after-free when the work executes after the wiphy data structure is freed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `cancel_work_sync(&rdev->rfkill_block);` in `wiphy_unregister()`, and the CVE/commit message directly states "The problem arises due to the rfkill_block work is not cancelled when wiphy is being unregistered." The KASAN report shows a use-after-free read in `cfg80211_shutdown_all_interfaces` called from `cfg80211_rfkill_block_work`, which is scheduled on a workqueue and runs after wiphy unregistration.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add cancellation of pending rfkill block work during wiphy unregister to prevent use-after-free race conditions.
intent_record.what: Added a call to cancel_work_sync(&rdev->rfkill_block) in wiphy_unregister before the existing cancel_work_sync(&rdev->conn_work).
intent_record.how: At runtime, during wiphy unregistration, the new line ensures that any pending or running rfkill block work is synchronously cancelled, preventing potential use-after-free or race conditions when the device is being removed.
